archdrw.archdrw:competition: 5185- 1977-64th lloyd warren fellowship, paris prize in architecture regeneration of an urban industrial neighborhood-2

panels.ocr_text: The neighborhood as a community is identifiable from surrounding areas. The general use districts are identifiable from within. The districts are tied to one another and to neighboring communities and parks by a pedestrian system, the main path being generated from the neighborhood core. The design allows an intermingling of diverse land uses while maintaining control on expansion and problems of interference. The neighborhood core becomes the central focus of the community, with a clear town center as the point of reference. It also identifies the neighborhood as a whole. The design encourages diversity and continuous activity in public plazas. Vehicular circulation is designed to lessen the impact of incompatible uses and to provide a transition between the residential and the commercial areas. Housing may be located in the core. This encourages diversity and continuous activity in public plazas. Development in the third phase calls for small-scale community and retail development. The neighborhood core will continue southward from the Market, which shapes the major link along a pedestrian path and will link the neighborhood core with the new residential development to the east.
panels.local_description: This panel includes a detailed map of the neighborhood core, circulation paths, and proposed phases of development.

panels.ocr_text: The desert defeats conventional perception of scale, space and form. Mountains rise abruptly from the desert floor, the river etches through rock and sand. The gorge reverses the polarity of the horizon line, making it a meaningless reference. The desert shifts across a sea of lava. A path is situated on it. The path becomes a polished seam of basalt reflecting the sky. It moves through a channel where the sky pierces the darkness through a slot. The intent is not to trivialize these phenomena by making them neatly understandable. The intent is to intensify the experience of the desert. There is no story, no beginnings, no end. The edge of the gorge is all there is.
panels.local_description: A conceptual drawing illustrating the Desert Passage project, highlighting the interplay of natural elements and human experience.

archdrw.archdrw:competition: 12456-1997-sun shelter an architectural design competition

panels.ocr_text: Our concept is to continue the movement of the ocean across the pier. We designed modular sun shading devices whose roof form expresses wave motion. Each module is a twenty-five foot wide unit long by twenty-five foot long and is composed of three elements: each trellis strips rest on bundled steel angles mounted on concrete bases. The weathering of the materials allows for flexibility in use, while its wave form as an expression of the spirit of the site.

panels.ocr_text: our proposal for the tkts2k ticket booth combines aspects of theater, landscape and signage to create an unconventional, yet appropriate, image for the Theatre Development Fund. not just a ticket booth, this proposal also gives Father Duffy Square a visible identity as an urban park for the general public. the building is composed of a light steel skeleton, which is prefabricated and brought to the site in sections. to the skeleton are attached glass-reinforced plastic panels with integral insulation, lighting, and mechanical systems. an elastomeric latex resin is used as cladding on all surfaces. as a theater, the project provides an elevated place from which to see and be seen. street performers can use the structure as a stage, while spectators of the perpetual performance that is Times Square can stroll up and enjoy balcony-like seating, as opposed to the overstimulating multimedia bombardment of most Times Square, which often leaves visitors alienated and disconnected from their surroundings, our proposal encourages human interaction and fosters spontaneous participation, breaking down barriers between spectator and spectacle. as a landscape, the project escorts ticket buyers on a journey in which, as they move through the queue, transforms Father Duffy Square from a glorified median into a public space in which can...

archdrw.archdrw:competition: 12786-2001-queens plaza an open ideas competition

panels.ocr_text: OPPORTUNISTIC ECOLOGIES This project is a form of successional urban ecology that exploits available niche environments in the urban infrastructure. The modular form and portability of the dumpster is suited to ad hoc occupation of empty parking spaces, creating street gardens. Community dumpster gardens colonize traffic islands and other void spaces. Simple initial forms evolve into complex adaptations of the bridge structures as vertical gardens.

THE SURFACE STRATEGY TO EXPLOIT THE HYPER-URBAN FLOW OR CIRCULATION OF MULTIPLE SURFACE LEVELS BY EXTENDING THE URBAN LANDSCAPE AS A PARALLEL PROGRAM. THIS NEW GROUND OPERATES AS A REINFORCED ACTIVE SURFACE. THE TRANSMISSION NETWORK ILLUSTRATES THE INTERCONNECTIONS BETWEEN THE VARIOUS LEVELS AND PROGRAMS, ENHANCING THE URBAN EXPERIENCE.

panels.panel_title: Waves on the Shore - Pavilion Design
panels.ocr_text: THIS PROJECT IS DEFINED BY THE INTERACTION OF SHAPES FOUND AT CONEY ISLAND. THE WAVES OF THE OCEAN, BOUND BY WATER AND LAND, TOGETHER GIVE BIRTH TO THE SITE AND ITS SHAPES. THE MISSHAPEN HURRICANE HAS COME TO REVEAL AND REDEFINE THE FORMS GIVEN TO AND FROM EACH LOCATION. IN DOING SO, THEY HAVE ALLOWED THE GROUND TO RISE IN FORM. THIS WAVE IS A REFLECTION OF SUPPORTING A MODERN AND HISTORIC EVENT.

panels.ocr_text: GATEWAY NATIONAL PARK Although it remains central to the way we think about our world, the conventional distinction between the natural and the man-made—between nature and the city—is no longer meaningful, and we cling to it at our peril. This project examines some of the physical, cultural, and social boundaries between New York City and Gateway National Park and proposes a series of strategies to make this relationship both more productive and more sustainable.

panels.ocr_text: The neighborhood as a community is identifiable from surrounding areas. The general use districts are identifiable from within. The districts are tied to one another and to neighboring communities and parks by a pedestrian system, the main path being generated from the neighborhood core. The design allows an intermingling of diverse land uses while maintaining control on expansion and problems of interference. The neighborhood core becomes the central focus of the community, with a clear town center as the point of reference. It also identifies the neighborhood as a whole. The design encourages diversity and continuous activity in public plazas. Vehicular circulation is designed to lessen the impact of incompatible uses and to provide a transition between the residential and the commercial areas. Housing may be located in the core. This encourages diversity and continuous activity in public plazas. Development in the third phase calls for small-scale community and retail development. The neighborhood core will continue southward from the Market, which shapes the major link along a pedestrian path and will link the neighborhood core with the new residential development to the east.
panels.local_description: This panel includes a detailed map of the neighborhood core, circulation paths, and proposed phases of development.

panels.ocr_text: The desert defeats conventional perception of scale, space and form. Mountains rise abruptly from the desert floor, the river etches through rock and sand. The gorge reverses the polarity of the horizon line, making it a meaningless reference. The desert shifts across a sea of lava. A path is situated on it. The path becomes a polished seam of basalt reflecting the sky. It moves through a channel where the sky pierces the darkness through a slot. The intent is not to trivialize these phenomena by making them neatly understandable. The intent is to intensify the experience of the desert. There is no story, no beginnings, no end. The edge of the gorge is all there is.
panels.local_description: A conceptual drawing illustrating the Desert Passage project, highlighting the interplay of natural elements and human experience.

panels.ocr_text: Our concept is to continue the movement of the ocean across the pier. We designed modular sun shading devices whose roof form expresses wave motion. Each module is a twenty-five foot wide unit long by twenty-five foot long and is composed of three elements: each trellis strips rest on bundled steel angles mounted on concrete bases. The weathering of the materials allows for flexibility in use, while its wave form as an expression of the spirit of the site.
panels.local_description: This component includes an axonometric view, partial plan, perspective view, and detailed sections of the sun shelter design.

panels.ocr_text: our proposal for the tkts2k ticket booth combines aspects of theater, landscape and signage to create an unconventional, yet appropriate, image for the Theatre Development Fund. not just a ticket booth, this proposal also gives Father Duffy Square a visible identity as an urban park for the general public. the building is composed of a light steel skeleton, which is prefabricated and brought to the site in sections. to the skeleton are attached glass-reinforced plastic panels with integral insulation, lighting, and mechanical systems. an elastomeric latex resin is used as cladding on all surfaces. as a theater, the project provides an elevated place from which to see and be seen. street performers can use the structure as a stage, while spectators of the perpetual performance that is Times Square can stroll up and enjoy balcony-like seating, as opposed to the overstimulating multimedia bombardment of most Times Square, which often leaves visitors alienated and disconnected from their surroundings, our proposal encourages human interaction and fosters spontaneous participation, breaking down barriers between spectator and spectacle. as a landscape, the project escorts ticket buyers on a journey in which, as they move through the queue, transforms Father Duffy Square from a glorified median into a public space in which can...

panels.panel_title: Waves on the Shore - Pavilion Design
panels.ocr_text: THIS PROJECT IS DEFINED BY THE INTERACTION OF SHAPES FOUND AT CONEY ISLAND. THE WAVES OF THE OCEAN, BOUND BY WATER AND LAND, TOGETHER GIVE BIRTH TO THE SITE AND ITS SHAPES. THE MISSHAPEN HURRICANE HAS COME TO REVEAL AND REDEFINE THE FORMS GIVEN TO AND FROM EACH LOCATION. IN DOING SO, THEY HAVE ALLOWED THE GROUND TO RISE IN FORM. THIS WAVE IS A REFLECTION OF SUPPORTING A MODERN AND HISTORIC EVENT.
